# Voice and speech AI architecture index

Canonical B2 product documentation: <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning>.

Use this index to choose a workflow. Each linked architecture states its evidence basis, what B2 is not in that workflow, and its security boundaries.

## [Voice training data lifecycle](../architectures/voice-training-data-lifecycle/architecture.md)

Collect speech with consent, validate and review it, and publish immutable dataset releases that NeMo, Lhotse, Hugging Face Datasets, WebDataset and MosaicML Streaming read from B2.

- **Audience:** ML engineers, Data engineers, Speech and audio researchers, Platform engineers
- **Problem:** Speech datasets need a record of consent per clip, repeatable validation, reviewed transcripts and versioned releases that training jobs in other locations can read and cite exactly.
- **Workflow:** Record consent in the protected zone -> Upload clips with presigned PUT URLs -> Validate and normalize on signed Event Notifications -> Review transcripts in Label Studio -> Build an immutable release with manifests and shards -> Read the release through a local cache for training
- **Expected scale:** From thousands of clips to multi-terabyte speech corpora. Collection and review run at any scale on standard B2. Training reads go through a local cache; B2 Overdrive applies only when sustained aggregate read throughput is the measured constraint.

## [Batch voice generation and dubbing](../architectures/batch-voice-generation-and-dubbing/architecture.md)

Send sources to dubbing, speech synthesis and transcription providers through presigned GET URLs, keep every output as an expiring candidate, and promote reviewed outputs to immutable deliveries with lineage.

- **Audience:** Backend engineers, Media pipeline engineers, ML engineers, Platform engineers
- **Problem:** Batch dubbing, speech synthesis and transcription jobs produce many outputs from hosted providers that return results through their own APIs; each output needs review, unused outputs must expire, and every delivered file must trace back to its source, job and consent.
- **Workflow:** Upload the source to the incoming zone -> Start a job on a signed Event Notification and check consent -> Submit the job with a presigned GET URL sized to the provider's download window -> Collect outputs on callback or by polling and copy them to candidates -> Review candidates through short-lived presigned URLs -> Promote approved outputs to an immutable delivery version with lineage -> Deliver through short-lived URLs or a private CDN while candidates expire
- **Expected scale:** From a few jobs a day to continuous batches of dubbing and transcription. Throughput is bound by the providers' job limits and the runner's concurrency, not by B2. Each output is stored at least twice while a candidate and its delivery coexist; candidate lifecycle bounds that overlap.

## [Voice agent session archive](../architectures/voice-agent-session-archive/architecture.md)

Archive finished voice agent sessions from LiveKit Egress or a session adapter, evaluate each session for quality and safety, retain it per class under Object Lock, and select only passed, consented sessions for review, analytics or datasets.

- **Audience:** Backend engineers, Voice agent developers, ML engineers, Platform engineers
- **Problem:** Voice agent platforms produce recordings, tracks, transcripts and events that must be kept for a defined period, traced to consent, and checked before anyone reuses them; most platforms do not write to B2 themselves.
- **Workflow:** Record the session with LiveKit Egress to B2, or copy it from the platform with an adapter -> Write the session manifest last, when the session has ended -> Start evaluation on a signed Event Notification for the manifest -> Run quality and safety checks and record the result and eligible uses -> Copy sessions to the protected zone with retention per class -> Retrieve sessions through short-lived presigned URLs issued by the application -> Select passed sessions whose consent covers the use into dataset releases
- **Expected scale:** From a few sessions a day to continuous call volume. Capture and archive scale with the platform's recording throughput, not with B2. Each retained session is stored twice until the incoming copy expires; the incoming lifecycle bounds that overlap.
